title: 9. Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes & No-FOMO Action Plan
book_title: Chapter 9: The Verdict and Capital Plan

epigraph.quote: Discipline is not predicting every molecule; it is refusing to pay 65 times free cash flow when the math and the market regime both say wait.
epigraph.author: Portfolio Committee

web_blocks.html: Before issuing a final capital verdict, we steelman both sides of the Eli Lilly debate using audited filings and live market data [33][34][35]. Our goal is to test whether a pullback to support earns a WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT queue or whether valuation and macro discipline demand an outright REJECTED call.

rows: Franchise & Volume
Q3 2026 volume jumped +53% YoY; 9M CFO doubled to $27.42B ($18.98B FCF); oral Foundayo & retatrutide extend obesity leadership [7][9][33][34]
65.9% revenue concentration in tirzepatide; -15% consolidated price erosion (-29% ex-U.S. China NRDL) signals intensifying payer pushback [33][34]

Valuation & Tape
Stage 2 VCP (13.24% BB width) above rising 50D ($1,267) and 30W ($1,194) SMAs; 27.0x Fwd P/E looks reasonable if 33% EPS growth holds [35][36]
65.5x P/FCF (1.53% yield vs 5.04% 10Y); even at $1,295.55 support, $1,450 Base Fair Value vs $1,172.53 stop yields just 1.26:1 (<1.50:1 gate) in a 10-dist-day Downtrend
web_blocks.takeaway: While Lilly's science and volume growth earn a COMPOUNDER_PASS, 65.5x P/FCF, -15% price erosion, $18.24B BD/M&A burn, and sub-1.50:1 support-zone asymmetry require rejecting new capital.

REJECTED (Valuation)

web_blocks.takeaway: Across short- and medium-term horizons, LLY is REJECTED on valuation and sub-1.50:1 asymmetry; long-term capital should stay patient until FCF multiples compress.

web_blocks.intro: LLY is NOT_HELD with zero shares and zero open options. At our $1,450.00 Base Fair Value, reward-to-risk is 0.59:1 at CMP and 1.26:1 at $1,295.55 support. Both fail our 1.50:1 gate, so the verdict is REJECTED (TIER_0, VALUATION). Our $1,172.53 reference stop sits strictly above the prior $1,158.45 stop.

web_blocks.html: Re-Underwriting Trigger (Do Not Buy Above $1,295): Keep new capital at $0 (REJECTED, TIER_0). Re-open underwriting only if LLY drops into the $1,050–$1,180 zone where $1,450 Base Fair Value offers at least 2.0:1 asymmetry AND filings verify that Acquired IPR&D normalizes below $5.0B/yr with consolidated net price erosion narrowing inside -5% YoY.

Consolidated U.S. cash sits at just $2,540.35 (3.38% of NAV) in a 10-distribution-day Downtrend [35]. Rejecting LLY protects this scarce liquidity. We earmark 100% of preserved watchlist capital to USD Cash / Short-Term T-Bills to rebuild toward the 22.0% floor (0% shortlist VRTX, which is Stage 3 and REJECTED in our 2026-11-20 batch; 0% outside equities).

book_paragraphs: When we place the bull and bear cases side by side, the tension is obvious. On the bullish side, Eli Lilly is executing one of the most remarkable commercial expansions in pharmaceutical history. Volume surged 53 percent in the third quarter, nine-month operating cash flow doubled to $27.42 billion, and oral Foundayo plus Phase 3 retatrutide give the company a credible multi-year runway.

On the bearish side, the market is asking us to pay 65.5 times free cash flow—a 1.53 percent cash yield—while the 10-year Treasury pays 5.04 percent. Meanwhile, tirzepatide concentration has climbed to 65.9 percent of revenue, realized net prices fell 15 percent in Q3, Trulicity and Verzenio enter 2028 Medicare price-setting, and management spent $18.24 billion on nine-month M&A and IPR&D while lifting gross debt to $49.50 billion.

To avoid hedging a great company at a poor price, we run the numbers through a strict probability-weighted outcome matrix. Assigning 25 percent weight to a $1,720 Bull Case, 50 percent weight to our $1,450 Base Case, and 25 percent weight to a stressed $1,050 Bear Case produces a 12-month Expected Value of $1,417.50 per share. From $1,347.11, that is just 5.2 percent expected upside against 13.0 percent downside to the $1,172.53 invalidation stop—a 0.40-to-1 ratio.

Even if LLY pulls back to the lower edge of its snapshot support zone at $1,295.55, a $1,450.00 Base Fair Value against a $1,172.53 stop offers only 1.26-to-1 reward-to-risk, falling short of our 1.50-to-1 minimum threshold. Consequently, we reject new capital deployment at Tier 0 on valuation grounds.

Walking through the three scenarios shows how little cushion exists at current prices. In our $1,450.00 Base Case at 48.0 times normalized 2027 free cash flow, investors earn 7.6 percent over twelve months. In our $1,050.00 Bear Case—driven by 20 percent GLP-1 price erosion and recurring Acquired IPR&D—the stock drops 22.1 percent. Combining those outcomes with our $1,720.00 Bull Case leaves a $1,417.50 Expected Value that fails our hurdle.

book_subsections.title: Action Plan and Capital Redeployment
paragraphs: Because we hold zero shares and zero options in Eli Lilly, no exit or trim execution is required. Our discipline is purely about keeping scarce capital out of harm's way while the U.S. market endures a ten-distribution-day Downtrend and our consolidated portfolio holds just $2,540.35 in cash, or 3.38 percent of net worth against a 22 percent Downtrend floor.

Rather than forcing capital into a 65.5x free-cash-flow mega-cap, we earmark 100 percent of preserved watchlist allocation to USD cash and Treasury bills to rebuild our liquidity buffer toward the 22 percent Downtrend floor. Shortlist peer VRTX is excluded (0 percent) because it sits in Stage 3 and is rejected in our November 20, 2026 batch, and outside equities remain at 0 percent.

Patience is an active position, not passive neglect. We will reopen Eli Lilly underwriting only if the stock corrects into the $1,050 to $1,180 range, where $1,450.00 Base Fair Value delivers at least 2.0-to-1 asymmetry. At the same time, future filings must show Acquired IPR&D normalizing below $5.0 billion per year and consolidated net price erosion narrowing inside minus 5 percent year-over-year. Until both conditions arrive, 100 percent USD cash remains the highest-conviction Downtrend posture.

callouts.title: Final Committee Verdict: REJECTED (TIER_0)
callouts.text: Hold 0 shares. Decline the $1,360/$1,640 call spread (1,240.4 bps of NAV). Allocate 100% of preserved capital to USD cash, and revisit LLY only on a correction into $1,050–$1,180 with Acquired IPR&D normalizing below $5B/yr.
